cells.tense: You are open to what the people around you are carrying, and it is landing.
cells.ask: Bring one shared thing — a phrase, a custom, a story — into words at the next gathering, say why it matters to you, then let someone add to it.
cells.core:
A friend says something in the circle and it reaches you before you decide to agree with it. You take it in, and you can still feel where you end and the others begin. That is the balance here: the meaning arrives, it moves you, and you stay yourself while it does.

On a good night this is quieter than it sounds. You notice something the group already holds, you name it without turning it into a speech, and you don't rush anyone toward agreement. The group finds out what it actually has because someone said so plainly, once. This week, offer one piece of that out loud. If the read is wrong, the thing you named is still in the room, and someone can still answer it.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a belonging that has not arrived yet.
cells.ask: At the next gathering, keep one piece of your own meaning to yourself and let the room move past it without you repairing the gap.
cells.core:
You feel your way into the group ahead of time — what they'll think, what they'll need, what the temperature will be — before anyone has said anything. You walk in already arranged. The room hasn't asked for any of it yet, and you've spent the hour rehearsing.

Getting a read on people isn't the problem. The problem is making the next room carry a version of itself that hasn't happened. On a good night, you arrive, you take people in, and you let that be enough for a while. This week, leave one silence alone rather than filling it early. Bring what you actually came with, not what you've already absorbed, and let the others arrive too.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Go to one shared thing with no role to play, and give the group one honest sentence about why you came.
cells.core:
You stepped back from letting a group's meaning reach you, and the step back worked — you kept your footing. Now things get passed around the room and you take them in from a distance. Nothing pushes you, and nothing quite arrives either. The receiving has gone quiet.

On a good night, you walk in with nothing to manage. No one to help, no temperature to fix, nothing to carry — just a person in a room where meaning is moving. This isn't something to force your way back into; the current comes on its own once you're standing in it. Pick one gathering and show up with no job. Then say one true thing about why you're there.

cells.tense: You are already keeping a meaning alive in how you speak, and calling it nobody's doing.
cells.ask: Name one thing you keep going for the group — a phrase, a custom, a story — and say plainly that you are the one keeping it.
cells.core:
You set the tone in a room without seeing yourself do it. Something gets passed on because you keep saying it, and you would describe that as just how things are done around here. That passing on is real. Calling it yours hasn't happened yet, and that's a small gap to close.

No speech required. Pick one thing you actually do — the phrase you repeat, the small custom you keep — and say out loud that it's yours. That takes nothing away from anyone. If the pick is wrong, saying it out loud still shows you where your own hands are in the room, which is the point.

attempts.check: The unsupported claims: the record doesn't say what the person needs from a group, how they read a room, or what recognition feels like to them; each cell only describes a capacity in a moment they'd recognize, never a universal. The reader could reasonably say the Too Little cell locates something behind them, so I kept that to a posture — standing at a door that closed — without saying what was there, who, or how long ago. The asks survive being wrong: each is a small outward gesture a camera could see, doable today, and teaches something whether or not my read matches. The sentence serving the writer — 'you already have a place in it, you just haven't said so' — I cut, because it flatters the reading rather than hands the person anything.
